# Mega Remediation: file issues + fix all the things (Sonnet-granular work packets)

## Context

A full diagnostic session (2026-07-01) root-caused "diarization doesn't work" to a **capture bug**: `CoreAudioTapCaptureActor` reads the input format once at setup (`CoreAudioTapCaptureActorSupport.swift:144`) and has no `AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange` observer, so a mid-session device sample-rate change makes the converter use a stale ratio — production WAVs are time-stretched 1.6–1.9×, corrupting transcription timestamps and diarization alignment. Two more production bugs surfaced: `-mic-cleaned.wav` files are pure digital silence (−180 dB), and `GRDBSQL.upsertSegment` never writes/clears `word_timings` (stale timings survive re-diarization).

The same session fixed all test suites (Record-ML now 314/314 green, uncommitted) and triaged ~55 open issues. Verification against main shows **several open issues are already fixed** (#190, #191, #193, #194, #205, most of F22) — they need regression-test-and-close, not fixes. The user folded **Epic 30** (#202, audit findings F1–F27 from `docs/codebase-audit-20260612-142636.md`) and the **contract-audit criticals** (#211–#213) into this plan. The prior Epic 30 plan (`~/.claude/plans/atomic-roaming-graham.md`) is the spec source for F-numbers but predates the GRDB migration — file paths below are corrected to current main.

**Goal**: every packet is small enough for a Sonnet agent to execute alone: one fix, explicit files, verify-first, TDD, one commit.

## Ground rules (embed in every agent prompt)

- **Scope**: touch ONLY the files listed in your packet. If the fix genuinely requires another file, stop and report back instead of editing it.
- **Verify first**: confirm the defect still exists on main before writing code. If already fixed, write the missing regression test (if any), then report `ALREADY_FIXED` with file:line evidence — do not "improve" working code.
- **TDD**: failing test first (RED), confirm failure via the package's `swift test --filter`, then implement (GREEN). Swift Testing (`@Test`/`#expect`), not XCTest.
- **Layering**: Domain → Foundation only; Business → Domain; Presentation never imports Infrastructure. File caps: Domain 100 / Business 300 / Infrastructure 300 / ViewModels 200 / Views 150 lines.
- **Impact check**: before editing a symbol, find its callers (`gitnexus_impact` if available, else grep) and list them in your report.
- **Commits**: one commit per fix, format `fix(scope): description (#issue)`. No Claude/Anthropic attribution. Never touch theme files (`Record-Presentation/Sources/Presentation/Theme/`, `Resources/`, `*Theme*Tests`).
- **gh**: always `unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh …`.
- **Tests per package**: `cd <pkg> && swift test` for Record-Foundation/Record-Audio/Record-ML; root `swift test` for the rest. Only ONE agent runs tests in a given package at a time (lane rule).
- **Model**: Sonnet for all packets unless marked `[main-loop]` (done by the orchestrator directly).

## Phase 0 — Bookkeeping `[main-loop]`

**0.1 Commit the session's uncommitted fixes** (before any agent edits, so packets diff cleanly):
- `fix(record-ml tests): monorepo paths, vacuous OSLog test, MCPLifecycle root + FD allowance` — 12 test files under `Record-ML/Tests/Unit/`
- `fix(record-ml): raise semantic cache threshold 0.10→0.55` — `CachingContextProvider.swift`, `SemanticCacheTests.swift`
- `fix(record-ml): isArmed accessor + poll-for-arm flake fix (#198)` — `CalendarAwareMeetingDetector.swift`, `CalendarAwareMeetingDetectorTests.swift`
- `refactor(record-ml): GRDBContextCache complexity` — `GRDBContextCache.swift`
- `test(record-ml): disable keychain access-group test pending entitlements (#125)` — `CredentialStoreTests.swift`
- Record-Foundation mocks/ISO8601, Record-Audio stale-path tests + AudioSessionDetector permission gate, Record-App `MockStorageEngine.swift` — one commit per package.
- **Leave uncommitted**: all Record-Presentation modified files (theme WIP intermixed) except after hunk-level review shows a purely-localization hunk; when ambiguous, skip.
- Then create branch `fix/mega-remediation-20260701` from main for all remaining work (local-only; no push/PR unless asked).

**0.2 File the three new issues** from `.temp/issue-drafts-20260701.md`: write the three body files it references, run its three `gh issue create` commands. Record the new issue numbers — packets A1, A6, M1 reference them.

**0.3 Post this plan as a comment on #202** (standing plans-to-GH-issues preference), noting Epic 30 is folded in.

## Wave 1 — Verify-and-close packets (parallel, read-mostly, cheap)

Each: confirm fix exists on main at the cited site, add a regression test **only if none exists**, comment evidence on the issue, close it (authorized).

| Packet | Issue | Evidence site on main | Regression test if missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| V1 | #190 AEC truncation | `AECProcessorActor.swift:125–170` remainder+chunk loop | `output.count == input.count` for 1,365-sample input |
| V2 | #191 ID mismatch | `StartRecordingUseCase.swift:119,127` single sessionID threaded | AudioFile.id == session.id assertion |
| V3 | #193 WAV deleted on DB fail | `StopAndTranscribeUseCase.swift:72–90` — deletes only on cancellation, preserves on storage throw | mock storage throws → file still exists |
| V4 | #194 silent converter errors | `ConverterErrorTracker` (CoreAudioTapCaptureActorSupport.swift:230) + `MicTapBridge.handleConverterError:109` | threshold-terminates stream |
| V5 | #205 symlink escape | `ObsidianProvider.swift:32–34` trailing-slash guard | symlinked file outside vault skipped |
| V6 | #189 + #138 stale test paths / FD flake | fixed in Phase 0 commits | none needed — cite commits |

## Wave 2 — Audio money path (Record-Audio lane, SERIAL — same files)

**A1 — System tap ignores mid-session sample-rate change (new issue from 0.2; THE diarization root cause).**
Files: `CoreAudioTapCaptureActor.swift`, `CoreAudioTapCaptureActorSupport.swift`, new `CoreAudioTapCaptureActorRouteChange.swift`, tests.
Mirror the #49 pattern from `MicCaptureActorRouteChange.swift:16–77` (`handleConfigurationChange()`): observe `.AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange` on the tap engine; on fire, remove tap, re-read `inputNode.inputFormat(forBus: 0)`, rebuild `AVAudioConverter` + tap closure (reuse continuation + writer + `tapT0`), restart engine. Defensive second layer: inside the tap callback compare `inBuffer.format.sampleRate` to the converter's assumed input rate; on mismatch log and trigger the rebuild (buffer's own format is authoritative). Remove observer in `cleanup()`. RED test: source-inspection test that the observer registration exists (behavioral CoreAudio tests can't run headless) + unit test of the ratio math via a rebuildable converter seam if feasible.

**A2 — #192 remainder: main tap WAVWriter has no errorHandler (F3).**
Files: `CoreAudioTapCaptureActor.swift:97–101`, test.
`WAVCleanedAudioSink` already wires it (F22 done, `errorHandler` is `public let`). Wire the tap's writer identically: handler finishes the session stream with `.writeFailed` and logs. Verify `_totalSamplesWritten` increments only on success (`WAVWriter.swift` ~99–130) — fix if not.

**A3 — F11: `stop()` duration from `wavWriter.totalSamplesWritten`, not wall clock.** Files: `CoreAudioTapCaptureActor.swift` (~:265). Remove `try? … ?? 0` / `?? Date()` silent fallbacks (DPS-204). Note: after A1 lands, samples-written is the honest duration even across rate changes.

**A4 — F27: create WAVWriter inside the `do` block** so failed starts don't orphan 44-byte WAVs. Files: `CoreAudioTapCaptureActor.swift:95–101` (note the existing `defer state` guard at :89–92 — keep it correct).

**A5 — #223: `abortRouteChange(with:)` dead code — wire it, don't delete it.**
Files: `MicCaptureActorRouteChange.swift`. It performs the *complete* cleanup (observer removal, voice-processing off, engine teardown) that `handleConfigurationChange()`'s three failure paths skip (they only set state + finish continuation, leaking observer/engine). Replace those failure paths with `abortRouteChange(with:)` calls. RED: source-inspection test that failure paths call it.

**A6 — Silent mic-cleaned WAV investigation (new issue from 0.2).**
Files: `AECProcessorActor.swift`, `WAVCleanedAudioSink.swift`, the far-end feed site (`RecordingStateViewModelStreaming.swift` — read-only for diagnosis), integration test file.
The writer chain is healthy (correct duration, errorHandler wired) — the silence enters upstream. Steps: (1) integration test: synthetic 440 Hz sine through `AECProcessorActor.process()` with silent far-end → assert non-zero output RMS; (2) same with far-end == mic signal (self-cancellation hypothesis) — if output goes to zero, the bug is the far-end wiring feeding mic as its own echo reference; (3) add a cheap guard in `AECProcessorActor`: log-once when N consecutive processed frames are all-zero while input RMS > threshold. Report findings; if the root cause is outside listed files, report back rather than fix.

**A7 — #198 remainder: fixed sleeps → polling** in `AudioSessionDetectorTests.swift:26`, `AudioSessionDetectorCoreAudioTests.swift:21` (Record-Audio) and `CalendarAwareMeetingDetectorTests.swift:130,166,201` (Record-ML — coordinate with ML lane). Build the F9 `waitForEvent(in:timeout:)` deadline helper (ContinuousClock) once per package; the `isArmed` polling pattern from Phase 0 is the model.

## Wave 3 — Record-ML lane (serial within lane; parallel to Wave 2)

**M1 — word_timings upsert gap (new issue from 0.2).** Files: `Record-ML/Sources/MLInfrastructure/Storage/GRDBSQL.swift:101–108`, `GRDBStorageActor+Diarization.swift:39–44`, tests. Add `word_timings` to `upsertSegment` (insert + `excluded` update), encode `seg.wordTimings` via `JSONEncoder` (nil → NULL) at the `attachDiarization` call site. RED: attach twice with different timings → second read returns second timings; attach with nil → NULL (not stale).

**M2 — #195/F6: FluidDiarizationPlugin re-entrancy.** Files: `FluidDiarizationPlugin.swift:167–188`, timeout test file. In-flight guard serializing `diarize()` (actor-state flag + `while` wait, or queue continuations); fix the misleading isolation comment at :163–165; cancel the detached task when `withTimeout` fires (currently orphaned). RED: two concurrent `diarize()` calls → second waits (no concurrent inference), timeout cancels underlying task.

**M3 — #197/F8: unmanaged `Task { await self.start() }` in init.** Files: `CalendarAwareMeetingDetector.swift` (init at ~:32). Store the handle, cancel in a `shutdown()`/`deinit`. Careful: Phase 0 added `isArmed` here — rebase on committed state.

**M4a — F13**: log the JSON parse error in `MCPSummarizationPlugin.swift` (~:179), not just the payload.
**M4b — F14**: missing prompt template throws at load instead of `?? ""` in `SummarizationPrompts.swift` (~:51).
**M4c — F15**: stop mapping every EventKit failure to `.accessDenied` in `Calendar/EventStore.swift` (~:20).
Three separate packets, one commit each.

**M5 — F12: failed ROLLBACK logging** — verify GRDB equivalent. GRDB's `dbPool.write` manages transactions itself; if no manual rollback exists anymore, report `OBSOLETE_POST_GRDB` and close the finding in the tracking comment.

**M6 — F23: atomic temp-file-rename writes** in `JSONSpeakerProfileStore.swift` (~:88–127).

**M7 — F16: honest `isPluggedIn`** via real power-source query (IOKit `IOPSCopyPowerSourcesInfo`) or `nil`, not `battery == 100`. `InferenceTelemetry.swift` (~:57).

**M8a — F24**: timeout errors read `TimeoutConfig` instead of hardcoded 300 — `WhisperKitPlugin.swift` (~:217), `WhisperKitProPlugin.swift` (~:195). **M8b — F25**: transcript-length log → `privacy: .private` in `AppleFoundationModelsPlugin.swift` (~:59).

## Wave 4 — App/Presentation/Pro lane (parallel to Waves 2–3)

**P1 — #196/F7: SearchViewModel generic catch** (`Record-Presentation/Sources/Presentation/ViewModels/SearchViewModel.swift` ~:53): set a generic `searchError` + log, clear stale prior error. RED: non-UserFacingError throw → error surfaced, not empty results.

**P2 — F17**: extract the shared ~140-line streaming loop from the two `transcribeStream` overloads in `StreamingTranscriptionUseCase.swift` (keep dropped-yield logging in both).

**P3 — F20 + #224 (Record-Pro)**: fix `PipelineRunner.swift:261–266` empty `rawResponse` debug dump (capture the real failed response or delete the path); delete dead `mergeSpeakers` at `PipelineRunner.swift:276` (verify zero callers first — issue said 3 copies, only 1 remains).

**P4 — F26 + warnings sweep**: delete `#expect(Bool(true))` tautologies (`MeetingAppMonitorTests.swift:59`, `AudioFileLoaderTests.swift:86`); fix `internal(set)` warning `MicCaptureActor.swift:38`; unused `meetingDetector` `AppAssemblerBuilders.swift:227`.

**P5 — F18: MenuBarViewModel split** (502 lines across 5 extension files → real units under the 200-line ViewModel cap). **P6 — F19: InferenceMetrics.swift split** (Domain 100-line cap). Both are refactors — run LAST in this lane, after P1–P4 commit, since they move code others reference.

## Wave 5 — MCP provider wiring (Unit E — sequenced, one packet per step)

Spec from the Epic 30 plan §Unit E with GRDB renames (`DuckDBContextCache` → `GRDBContextCache`, already exists and was refactored in Phase 0):
1. **E1** `NotionProvider.isHealthy()` three-way fix (nil credential → false; `keychainReadFailed` logged distinctly → false; optional 3s `GET /v1/users/me` ping). Keep `Bool`.
2. **E2** Cache provider-scoping: add `provider_id` to exact + semantic get/put in `GRDBContextCache` + `GRDBSQL` cache statements; `CachingContextProvider` passes `inner.providerID`. RED: cross-provider isolation test. (Build on the 0.55-threshold work from Phase 0.)
3. **E3** `AppConfig` fields `obsidianVaultPath: String?`, `notionEnabled = false` (`decodeIfPresent`; update memberwise-copy sites in `Record-App/Sources/TheRecord/App.swift`). **Pre-check**: if the app is sandboxed (check entitlements), vault path must be a security-scoped bookmark `Data` — report before implementing.
4. **E4** Wire in `AppAssembler.buildMCPProviders` (`AppAssemblerBuilders.swift` ~:141): `KeychainCredentialStore` + `migrateAccessibilityIfNeeded()`, `GRDBContextCache` at `Directories.appSupport` when `config.contextCache.enabled`, wrap every provider in `CachingContextProvider`; degrade to uncached on cache-init throw.
5. **E5** Settings "Integrations" tab: consumer-side `IntegrationSettingsStore` protocol in Presentation (layer rule), adapter at composition root; Notion toggle + SecureField, Obsidian folder picker, "Test connection" button. Restart-required v1.
6. **E6** Integration test: ObsidianProvider against temp vault through full `QueryContextUseCase` chain; cache hit on second query (`RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1`).

## Wave 6 — Contract-audit criticals (#211–#213) — after Wave 5 (E4 touches the same assembler)

Each packet starts by reading its issue body (`unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh issue view <n>`), which is the spec:
- **C1 — #211 DiskSpaceMonitor**: dead feature, zero production implementation → implement + wire (aligns with GA #124 storage guard; minimal v1: warn below threshold before recording start).
- **C2 — #212 ModelDownloadDelegate**: unwired delegate → connect download progress to the consuming view model.
- **C3 — #213 PrivacyModeProvider**: 11 consumers get nil → wire a real provider at the composition root (default `PrivacyMode.default`).

## Wave 7 — Verification & review `[main-loop orchestrated]`

1. **Full suites, ratchet-only**: `Record-Foundation`, `Record-Audio`, `Record-ML` (baseline 314/49 green), root package. Known allowed failure: root `MiscLintTests` ThemeEditorView 786>500 (theme WIP, explicitly deprioritized — do not fix).
2. **3-round adversarial review** (user's standing pattern): Round 1 per-lane reviewers (audio / ML / app+presentation / MCP), Round 2 cross-dimensional (concurrency, layering, silent-failure), Round 3 one mega-adversary trying to disprove the two headline fixes (A1 rate-change, A6 silence) with a synthesizer verdict. Sonnet agents; findings → fix packets or logged.
3. **Re-run the epic-28 AEC verification harness** after A6 (epic-28 numbers were measured with #190 in place) — update CHANGELOG/CURRENT_STATE numbers if present.
4. `swiftlint` clean on touched files; `gitnexus_detect_changes()` before final commits if index is fresh.
5. Close issues fixed by this work with evidence comments: #192, #195, #196, #197, #198, #211, #212, #213, #223, #224, the three new issues, plus Wave 1's closures. Comment progress on #202.

## Orchestration mechanics

- **Canary first** (pre-flight rule): run V5 (#205 verify-and-close, smallest packet) alone; on success launch the rest of Wave 1 in parallel, then start lanes.
- Lanes = packages; packets within a lane run serially (build-dir + file contention), lanes run in parallel (max 4 concurrent agents).
- Agents get: the ground-rules block, their packet spec verbatim, exact file paths, and the package test command. `model: sonnet` on every Agent call.
- Orchestrator (main loop) reviews each agent's report + diff before the next packet in that lane starts; failed packets get one retry with the error trace, then escalate to Opus/main-loop.
- Everything stays local on `fix/mega-remediation-20260701` — no push/PR unless the user asks.

## Estimate

~35 packets: 6 verify-and-close, ~20 small fixes, A1/A6/E-series/C-series meaty. Largest risks: A1 (CoreAudio, hard to test headless — lean on the proven #49 pattern), E5 (new UI, layer discipline), C1–C3 (spec lives in issue bodies).

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- codex:codex-rescue: Proactively use when Claude Code is stuck, wants a second implementation or diagnosis pass, needs a deeper root-cause investigation, or should hand a substantial coding task to Codex through the shared runtime (Tools: Bash)

- entire-search: Search Entire checkpoint history and transcripts with `entire search --json`. Use proactively when the user asks about previous work, commits, sessions, prompts, or historical context in this repository. (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- hookify:conversation-analyzer: Use this agent when analyzing conversation transcripts to find behaviors worth preventing with hooks. Typical triggers include the /hookify command being invoked without arguments, or the user explicitly asking to look back at the current conversation and surface mistakes that should be prevented in the future. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: Read, Grep)
- performance-monitor: Monitor agent execution, track token usage, measure response quality, and optimize workflows (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep)

- seo-content: Content quality reviewer. Evaluates E-E-A-T signals, readability, content depth, AI citation readiness, and thin content detection. (Tools: Read, Bash, Write, Grep)
- seo-performance: Performance analyzer. Measures and evaluates Core Web Vitals and page load performance. (Tools: Read, Bash, Write)
- seo-schema: Schema markup expert. Detects, validates, and generates Schema.org structured data in JSON-LD format. (Tools: Read, Bash, Write)
- seo-sitemap: Sitemap architect. Validates XML sitemaps, generates new ones with industry templates, and enforces quality gates for location pages. (Tools: Read, Bash, Write, Glob)

- seo-technical: Technical SEO specialist. Analyzes crawlability, indexability, security, URL structure, mobile optimization, Core Web Vitals, and JavaScript rendering. (Tools: Read, Bash, Write, Glob, Grep)
- seo-visual: Visual analyzer. Captures screenshots, tests mobile rendering, and analyzes above-the-fold content using Playwright. (Tools: Read, Bash, Write)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service -- even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer -- your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.

## serena
CRITICAL: Before starting to work on a coding task, call the `initial_instructions` tool to read the 'Serena Instructions Manual'.

## tokensave
tokensave is a code-graph MCP server. Start with tokensave_context for any code exploration task — it returns relevant symbols, relationships, and code snippets for a natural-language query. Use tokensave_search to find specific symbols by name. Discovery and analysis tools are read-only and safe to call in parallel. Edit and session-memory tools can mutate local project state and declare readOnlyHint=false. When a tool result contains a `tokensave_metrics:` line, report the savings to the user (e.g. 'TokenSave\'d ~N tokens').

name: feedback-workflow-rate-limiting
description: Chunk parallel() fan-outs in Workflow scripts to avoid provider rate-limit bursts
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When authoring Workflow scripts, avoid firing large unbounded `parallel()` arrays or barrier-free `pipeline()` fan-outs that can stack many concurrent agent() calls (e.g. 5 Sonnet "find" lenses each spawning several parallel Haiku "verify" calls simultaneously) — this bursts past provider rate limits (429/overloaded_error) even though the workflow's own concurrency cap doesn't prevent it.

**Why:** User flagged this after launching a 5-lens adversarial pre-mortem workflow (mega-remediation-premortem, 2026-07-01) that fanned out Find (5x Sonnet) + Verify (per-finding Haiku, no barrier between lenses) — saw rate-limit errors in the live `/workflows` view. On inspection the journal showed 0 actual dead agents (no `result: null`) — the harness's automatic retry absorbed the 429s — but the burst pattern itself was the root cause worth fixing prospectively, not just tolerating.

**How to apply:** When writing a Workflow script with a fan-out stage of unknown/large size (e.g. verify-each-finding, one-per-file), chunk the `parallel()` calls into small batches (3-4 at a time, awaited sequentially) rather than mapping the whole array into one `parallel()`. Prefer this by default for any stage that could produce more than ~6-8 concurrent agent() calls at once. Confirmed preference: for an already-running workflow with no actual failures, let it finish rather than kill/restart — only throttle in scripts written from that point forward.

# Issue drafts — 2026-07-01 session (blocked from filing; run manually if approved)

## Draft 1 — THE diarization root cause

```bash
unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh issue create \
  --title "[see-something] correctness: system tap ignores mid-session sample-rate changes — WAV timeline stretched ~1.6-1.9x, breaks diarization + transcript timestamps (CoreAudioTapCaptureActorSupport.swift:144)" \
  --label "see-something" \
  --body-file .temp/issue-body-tap-rate.md
```

### Body (`.temp/issue-body-tap-rate.md`)

**What's wrong.** `CoreAudioTapCaptureActor` captures `inputFormat = newEngine.inputNode.inputFormat(forBus: 0)` once during `setupAggregateAndEngine` (CoreAudioTapCaptureActorSupport.swift:144) and derives the AVAudioConverter ratio from it (`ratio = configuration.sampleRate / inputFormat.sampleRate`). There is **no `AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange` observer on this engine** — unlike `MicCaptureActor`, which got exactly this handling in #49 (`MicCaptureActorRouteChange.swift`). When the tapped output device changes sample rate mid-session (e.g. Bluetooth headset renegotiating A2DP↔HFP when the mic engages — which THE RECORD itself triggers via `MicCaptureActor`), the tap keeps delivering buffers at the new rate while the converter still assumes the old one → time-stretched WAV.

**Evidence (production data, ~/Library/Application Support/THE RECORD).** Recording `F7C8DEAE-18DF-4853-B0D0-313FB81860BC` (2026-06-22): file birth→mtime 14:25:03→14:25:34 = **31 s wall time** (DB duration 31.195 s, mic-cleaned file 29.856 s — both agree), but main WAV `2026-06-22T20:25:03Z.wav` holds **57.685 s** @16 kHz (922,960 frames) = **1.85× wall time**. Signal analysis: zero duplicated blocks, no long-lag self-similarity (a 1 s probe matches only itself), pitch **bimodal** (~99 Hz and ~186 Hz clusters) → part of the session is rate-stretched, part normal → the rate changed mid-session. Second recording `F34D479A` (2026-06-18): WAV 10.085 s vs 6.23 s wall = **1.62×** — ratio varies with when the change occurred.

**Why it matters.** The main WAV is the single source of truth for the pipeline: batch transcription produces degraded text with timestamps on a fake 0–57.7 s timeline; diarization aligns speaker boundaries to that same corrupted audio (observed segments alternate "1"/"Unknown" across 0–57.68 s for a 31 s session). **This is the root cause of "diarization doesn't work."**

**Suggested fix.** Mirror the #49 fix on the system-tap engine: (1) observe `.AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange`, re-read `inputNode.inputFormat(forBus: 0)`, rebuild the converter+tap; (2) defensively compare `inBuffer.format.sampleRate` against the assumed rate inside the tap callback and rebuild on mismatch — the buffer's own format is authoritative; (3) log the change (relates to #194 — converter errors in this callback are currently silent).

Related: #49 (same bug fixed for MicCaptureActor), #194.

## Draft 2 — silent mic-cleaned WAV

```bash
unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh issue create \
  --title "[see-something] correctness: mic-cleaned WAV is pure digital silence in production — AEC/sink chain writes no signal (AECProcessorActor.swift, WAVCleanedAudioSink)" \
  --label "see-something" \
  --body-file .temp/issue-body-silent-mic.md
```

### Body (`.temp/issue-body-silent-mic.md`)

**What's wrong.** Both production `-mic-cleaned.wav` files (2026-06-18, 2026-06-22) contain **no signal at all**: average spectrum is −180 dB across every band 0–8 kHz. The file has the right duration (≈ wall time) but every sample is zero. So the mic → AEC → `CleanedAudioSink` chain runs, paces correctly, and writes silence.

**Why it matters.** The cleaned-mic track exists to feed the cleanup re-transcription pass (`cleaned_mic_audio_url`, `needs_retranscription`); a silent file means that pass transcribes nothing and the user's own voice is lost from the archive. Likely interacts with #190 (AEC truncates every mic buffer to 256 samples) and #192 (WAVWriter errorHandler never wired — failures invisible).

**Suggested fix.** Instrument the AEC output path with an RMS check (log if N consecutive cleaned buffers are all-zero); verify SpeexDSP echo-cancellation state isn't cancelling the entire near-end signal (e.g. mic signal fed as both near and far end); add an integration test asserting non-zero RMS through `AECProcessorActor` for a synthetic voice buffer.

Related: #190, #192, #231 (WAVCleanedAudioSink coupling).

## Draft 3 — stale word_timings on re-diarization

```bash
unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh issue create \
  --title "[see-something] silent-bug: attachDiarization upsert never clears word_timings — stale timings survive re-diarization (GRDBStorageActor+Diarization.swift:40)" \
  --label "see-something" \
  --body-file .temp/issue-body-word-timings.md
```

### Body (`.temp/issue-body-word-timings.md`)

**What's wrong.** `attachDiarization` upserts segments via `GRDBSQL.upsertSegment`, whose `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` sets text/speaker/start/end/confidence but **not `word_timings`** — and `DiarizedSegment.wordTimings` from the incoming transcript is never written. `getSegments` reads `word_timings` back and attaches it to whatever text now occupies that `segment_index`.

**Why it matters.** After any re-diarization (repair pipeline, cleanup pass), segment N's text/boundaries change but its old `word_timings` JSON remains → word-level highlighting/alignment silently points at the wrong words.

**Suggested fix.** Either persist `seg.wordTimings` in the upsert (add the column to `upsertSegment` with excluded update), or explicitly `SET word_timings = NULL` on conflict so stale data can't survive.

input.content:
**What's wrong.** `CoreAudioTapCaptureActor` captures `inputFormat = newEngine.inputNode.inputFormat(forBus: 0)` once during `setupAggregateAndEngine` (CoreAudioTapCaptureActorSupport.swift:144) and derives the AVAudioConverter ratio from it (`ratio = configuration.sampleRate / inputFormat.sampleRate`). There is **no `AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange` observer on this engine** — unlike `MicCaptureActor`, which got exactly this handling in #49 (`MicCaptureActorRouteChange.swift`). When the tapped output device changes sample rate mid-session (e.g. Bluetooth headset renegotiating A2DP↔HFP when the mic engages — which THE RECORD itself triggers via `MicCaptureActor`), the tap keeps delivering buffers at the new rate while the converter still assumes the old one → time-stretched WAV.

**Evidence (production data, ~/Library/Application Support/THE RECORD).** Recording `F7C8DEAE-18DF-4853-B0D0-313FB81860BC` (2026-06-22): file birth→mtime 14:25:03→14:25:34 = **31 s wall time** (DB duration 31.195 s, mic-cleaned file 29.856 s — both agree), but main WAV `2026-06-22T20:25:03Z.wav` holds **57.685 s** @16 kHz (922,960 frames) = **1.85× wall time**. Signal analysis: zero duplicated blocks, no long-lag self-similarity (a 1 s probe matches only itself), pitch **bimodal** (~99 Hz and ~186 Hz clusters) → part of the session is rate-stretched, part normal → the rate changed mid-session. Second recording `F34D479A` (2026-06-18): WAV 10.085 s vs 6.23 s wall = **1.62×** — ratio varies with when the change occurred.

**Why it matters.** The main WAV is the single source of truth for the pipeline: batch transcription produces degraded text with timestamps on a fake 0–57.7 s timeline; diarization aligns speaker boundaries to that same corrupted audio (observed segments alternate "1"/"Unknown" across 0–57.68 s for a 31 s session). **This is the root cause of "diarization doesn't work."**

**Suggested fix.** Mirror the #49 fix on the system-tap engine: (1) observe `.AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange`, re-read `inputNode.inputFormat(forBus: 0)`, rebuild the converter+tap; (2) defensively compare `inBuffer.format.sampleRate` against the assumed rate inside the tap callback and rebuild on mismatch — the buffer's own format is authoritative; (3) log the change (relates to #194 — converter errors in this callback are currently silent).

Related: #49 (same bug fixed for MicCaptureActor), #194.

**What's wrong.** Both production `-mic-cleaned.wav` files (2026-06-18, 2026-06-22) contain **no signal at all**: average spectrum is −180 dB across every band 0–8 kHz. The file has the right duration (≈ wall time) but every sample is zero. So the mic → AEC → `CleanedAudioSink` chain runs, paces correctly, and writes silence.

**Why it matters.** The cleaned-mic track exists to feed the cleanup re-transcription pass (`cleaned_mic_audio_url`, `needs_retranscription`); a silent file means that pass transcribes nothing and the user's own voice is lost from the archive. Likely interacts with #190 (AEC truncates every mic buffer to 256 samples) and #192 (WAVWriter errorHandler never wired — failures invisible).

**Suggested fix.** Instrument the AEC output path with an RMS check (log if N consecutive cleaned buffers are all-zero); verify SpeexDSP echo-cancellation state isn't cancelling the entire near-end signal (e.g. mic signal fed as both near and far end); add an integration test asserting non-zero RMS through `AECProcessorActor` for a synthetic voice buffer.

Related: #190, #192, #231 (WAVCleanedAudioSink coupling).

input.content:
**What's wrong.** `attachDiarization` upserts segments via `GRDBSQL.upsertSegment`, whose `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` sets text/speaker/start/end/confidence but **not `word_timings`** — and `DiarizedSegment.wordTimings` from the incoming transcript is never written. `getSegments` reads `word_timings` back and attaches it to whatever text now occupies that `segment_index`.

**Why it matters.** After any re-diarization (repair pipeline, cleanup pass), segment N's text/boundaries change but its old `word_timings` JSON remains → word-level highlighting/alignment silently points at the wrong words.

**Suggested fix.** Either persist `seg.wordTimings` in the upsert (add the column to `upsertSegment` with excluded update), or explicitly `SET word_timings = NULL` on conflict so stale data can't survive.

- **Scope**: touch ONLY the files listed in your packet. If the fix genuinely requires another file, stop and report back instead of editing it.
- **Verify first**: confirm the defect still exists on main before writing code. If already fixed, write the missing regression test (if any), then report `ALREADY_FIXED` with file:line evidence — do not "improve" working code.
- **Independent spot-check before closing on ALREADY_FIXED/OBSOLETE**: a second agent (or the orchestrator directly) re-reads the cited file:line evidence and re-runs the regression test independently, without seeing the first agent's conclusion beforehand, before any issue is closed on an `ALREADY_FIXED`, `OBSOLETE_POST_GRDB`, or similar verdict. If the second check disagrees, treat it as a normal packet failure — reopen with the discrepancy and route to a new fix packet, do not close.
- **TDD**: failing test first (RED), confirm failure via the package's `swift test --filter`, then implement (GREEN). Swift Testing (`@Test`/`#expect`), not XCTest.
- **Layering**: Domain → Foundation only; Business → Domain; Presentation never imports Infrastructure. File caps: Domain 100 / Business 300 / Infrastructure 300 / ViewModels 200 / Views 150 lines.
- **Impact check**: before editing a symbol, find its callers (`gitnexus_impact` if available, else grep) and list them in your report.
- **Commits**: one commit per fix, format `fix(scope): description (#issue)`. No Claude/Anthropic attribution. Never touch theme files (`Record-Presentation/Sources/Presentation/Theme/`, `Resources/`, `*Theme*Tests`).
- **gh**: always `unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh …`.
- **Tests per package**: `cd <pkg> && swift test` for Record-Foundation/Record-Audio/Record-ML; root `swift test` for the rest. Only ONE agent runs tests in a given package at a time (lane rule).
- **Model**: Sonnet for all packets unless marked `[main-loop]` (done by the orchestrator directly).

## Pre-execution adversarial findings (fleet pre-mortem, 2026-07-01)

A fleet of adversarial reviewers pre-mortemed this plan before execution started. Every finding below was independently verified against current main. Fixes are applied inline at each packet's bullet below (search for "Pre-flight (fleet pre-mortem)"); this section is the index.

- **P4 & E4**: Both packets edit `AppAssemblerBuilders.swift` in different functions (P4 at `:227` inside `buildMenuBarVM`, E4 at `:128` inside `buildMCPProviders`), but Wave 4 is only marked "parallel to Waves 2–3" — the plan's only cross-wave collision note covers Wave 6 → Wave 5 (E4), not Wave 4 (P4) → Wave 5 (E4). Fix: P4 must land (commit) before E4 starts even though their lanes are otherwise parallel.
- **A7 & M3**: A7 (Wave 2/Audio lane) edits `CalendarAwareMeetingDetectorTests.swift` while M3 (Wave 3/ML lane, parallel to Wave 2) simultaneously changes the task-lifecycle of the class under test — "coordinate with ML lane" is not an enforceable scheduling rule. Fix: moved the ML-side portion of A7 into Wave 3 as new packet M3b, sequenced immediately after M3, so the ML lane owns both the actor and its test.
- **A2/A3/A4**: Their cited line numbers in `CoreAudioTapCaptureActor.swift` are a pre-A1 snapshot; A1 (same serial lane, runs first) inserts new observer-registration/rebuild code that will shift every subsequent line number, and the plan never says so. Fix: added a note to the Wave 2 header instructing A2–A7 to re-locate cited code by symbol/content once A1 has landed, not by the literal line numbers in this plan.
- **E4**: `AppAssembler.buildMCPProviders` already implements most of the E4 spec (KeychainCredentialStore + migrateAccessibilityIfNeeded, degrade-on-throw GRDBContextCache, CachingContextProvider wrap-all, conditional Notion/Obsidian), and the cited line was wrong (`~141` vs actual `:128`). Fix: corrected the citation to `:128–172` and added a pre-flight callout to verify against `AppAssemblerMCPWiringTests` (E4a–E4d) before implementing; the one real gap left is that cache construction isn't gated on `config.contextCache.enabled` and uses `databasePath: nil` instead of `Directories.appSupport`.
- **E1**: `NotionProvider.isHealthy()` already implements the exact three-way fix (nil credential → false, Keychain-read-failure logged distinctly → false, 3s ping to `/v1/users/me`) and is already covered by `NotionProviderTests.swift:171–221`. Fix: re-scoped E1 to verify-and-close citing `NotionProvider.swift:80–108`.
- **M7**: `InferenceTelemetry` already implements honest `isPluggedIn` via a real IOKit power-source query (`queryIsPluggedIn()` at `:103–117`, wired at `:58`); no `battery == 100` code exists anywhere in the file. Fix: re-scoped M7 to verify-and-close with the corrected citation.
- **E3**: `AppConfig.notionEnabled`/`obsidianVaultPath` already exist and are already covered by `AppConfigTests.swift:334–380` (E3-named tests) — but this does NOT make E3 a pure verify-and-close: the app is confirmed sandboxed (`bodyman-entitlements.plist:5`) and `obsidianVaultPath` is confirmed still a plain `String?`, not a security-scoped bookmark. Fix: the packet's existing mandatory pre-check must actually be executed (convert to bookmark `Data`), not skipped.
- **M4b**: `SummarizationPrompts.loadTemplate` already throws (`SummarizationError.missingTemplate`) on a missing template with no `?? ""` fallback anywhere in the function, and is already covered by `SummarizationPromptsTests.swift:84`; the cited line (`~51`) pointed at a blank line past the real throw site. Fix: re-scoped M4b to verify-and-close citing `SummarizationPrompts.swift:48` and the test at `:84`.

6. **Verdict**: **ALREADY_FIXED** — guard was already correct and shipped on main; added a missing behavioral regression test to close the coverage gap the plan flagged.</result>

**What's wrong.** `attachDiarization` upserts segments via `GRDBSQL.upsertSegment`, whose `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` sets text/speaker/start/end/confidence but **not `word_timings`** — and `DiarizedSegment.wordTimings` from the incoming transcript is never written. `getSegments` reads `word_timings` back and attaches it to whatever text now occupies that `segment_index`.

**Why it matters.** After any re-diarization (repair pipeline, cleanup pass), segment N's text/boundaries change but its old `word_timings` JSON remains → word-level highlighting/alignment silently points at the wrong words.

**Suggested fix.** Either persist `seg.wordTimings` in the upsert (add the column to `upsertSegment` with excluded update), or explicitly `SET word_timings = NULL` on conflict so stale data can't survive.

**What's wrong.** Both production `-mic-cleaned.wav` files (2026-06-18, 2026-06-22) contain **no signal at all**: average spectrum is −180 dB across every band 0–8 kHz. The file has the right duration (≈ wall time) but every sample is zero. So the mic → AEC → `CleanedAudioSink` chain runs, paces correctly, and writes silence.

**Why it matters.** The cleaned-mic track exists to feed the cleanup re-transcription pass (`cleaned_mic_audio_url`, `needs_retranscription`); a silent file means that pass transcribes nothing and the user's own voice is lost from the archive. Likely interacts with #190 (AEC truncates every mic buffer to 256 samples) and #192 (WAVWriter errorHandler never wired — failures invisible).

**Suggested fix.** Instrument the AEC output path with an RMS check (log if N consecutive cleaned buffers are all-zero); verify SpeexDSP echo-cancellation state isn't cancelling the entire near-end signal (e.g. mic signal fed as both near and far end); add an integration test asserting non-zero RMS through `AECProcessorActor` for a synthetic voice buffer.

Related: #190, #192, #231 (WAVCleanedAudioSink coupling).

**What's wrong.** `CoreAudioTapCaptureActor` captures `inputFormat = newEngine.inputNode.inputFormat(forBus: 0)` once during `setupAggregateAndEngine` (CoreAudioTapCaptureActorSupport.swift:144) and derives the AVAudioConverter ratio from it (`ratio = configuration.sampleRate / inputFormat.sampleRate`). There is **no `AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange` observer on this engine** — unlike `MicCaptureActor`, which got exactly this handling in #49 (`MicCaptureActorRouteChange.swift`). When the tapped output device changes sample rate mid-session (e.g. Bluetooth headset renegotiating A2DP↔HFP when the mic engages — which THE RECORD itself triggers via `MicCaptureActor`), the tap keeps delivering buffers at the new rate while the converter still assumes the old one → time-stretched WAV.

**Evidence (production data, ~/Library/Application Support/THE RECORD).** Recording `F7C8DEAE-18DF-4853-B0D0-313FB81860BC` (2026-06-22): file birth→mtime 14:25:03→14:25:34 = **31 s wall time** (DB duration 31.195 s, mic-cleaned file 29.856 s — both agree), but main WAV `2026-06-22T20:25:03Z.wav` holds **57.685 s** @16 kHz (922,960 frames) = **1.85× wall time**. Signal analysis: zero duplicated blocks, no long-lag self-similarity (a 1 s probe matches only itself), pitch **bimodal** (~99 Hz and ~186 Hz clusters) → part of the session is rate-stretched, part normal → the rate changed mid-session. Second recording `F34D479A` (2026-06-18): WAV 10.085 s vs 6.23 s wall = **1.62×** — ratio varies with when the change occurred.

**Why it matters.** The main WAV is the single source of truth for the pipeline: batch transcription produces degraded text with timestamps on a fake 0–57.7 s timeline; diarization aligns speaker boundaries to that same corrupted audio (observed segments alternate "1"/"Unknown" across 0–57.68 s for a 31 s session). **This is the root cause of "diarization doesn't work."**

**Suggested fix.** Mirror the #49 fix on the system-tap engine: (1) observe `.AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange`, re-read `inputNode.inputFormat(forBus: 0)`, rebuild the converter+tap; (2) defensively compare `inBuffer.format.sampleRate` against the assumed rate inside the tap callback and rebuild on mismatch — the buffer's own format is authoritative; (3) log the change (relates to #194 — converter errors in this callback are currently silent).

Related: #49 (same bug fixed for MicCaptureActor), #194.

name: feedback-workflow-rate-limiting
description: Chunk parallel() fan-outs in Workflow scripts to avoid provider rate-limit bursts
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 7c35d465-d5ef-477e-a940-9baf3548f83d
---

When authoring Workflow scripts, avoid firing large unbounded `parallel()` arrays or barrier-free `pipeline()` fan-outs that can stack many concurrent agent() calls (e.g. 5 Sonnet "find" lenses each spawning several parallel Haiku "verify" calls simultaneously) — this bursts past provider rate limits (429/overloaded_error) even though the workflow's own concurrency cap doesn't prevent it.

**Why:** User flagged this after launching a 5-lens adversarial pre-mortem workflow (mega-remediation-premortem, 2026-07-01) that fanned out Find (5x Sonnet) + Verify (per-finding Haiku, no barrier between lenses) — saw rate-limit errors in the live `/workflows` view. On inspection the journal showed 0 actual dead agents (no `result: null`) — the harness's automatic retry absorbed the 429s — but the burst pattern itself was the root cause worth fixing prospectively, not just tolerating.

**How to apply:** When writing a Workflow script with a fan-out stage of unknown/large size (e.g. verify-each-finding, one-per-file), chunk the `parallel()` calls into small batches (3-4 at a time, awaited sequentially) rather than mapping the whole array into one `parallel()`. Prefer this by default for any stage that could produce more than ~6-8 concurrent agent() calls at once. Confirmed preference: for an already-running workflow with no actual failures, let it finish rather than kill/restart — only throttle in scripts written from that point forward.

[see-something] tests: meta-tests hardcode pre-monorepo source paths — fail when suites run per-package (Record-Audio/Tests/Unit/*)
## What's wrong

Several Record-Audio meta-tests (lint-style tests that Read source files and assert on their contents) hardcode paths from before the monorepo move and fail with NSCocoaErrorDomain 260 (file not found) when the suite runs via `cd Record-Audio && swift test`:

- `AVFoundationExportActorTests.swift:32` → looks for `/Volumes/Extra/repos/gitrdunhq/Sources/Infrastructure/Audio/AVFoundationExportActor.swift` (missing the-record-suite segment entirely)
- `WaveformProcessorTests.swift:171` → `<repo>/Sources/Infrastructure/Audio/WaveformProcessor.swift` (missing Record-Audio/ prefix)
- `AudioSessionDetectorTests.swift:96,101` → same pattern
- `WAVWriterRaceTests.swift:226` → same pattern

Observed in epic-28 validate: 5 failures in an otherwise green 77-test partial run (.temp/record-audio-suite.log).

## Why it matters

These are the suite's architecture-enforcement tests (actor declarations, NSLock usage, no-sync-in-finalize). They silently can't enforce anything when run per-package — and per-package is the only way to run these suites at all, since root `swift test --filter` matches 0 tests for sub-package suites (see AGENTS.md gotcha). Same disease as #36 (test.py REPO_ROOT), different host.

## Suggested fix

Resolve source paths from `#filePath` of the test file (walk up to the package root, then `Sources/...`) instead of repo-root-relative literals — that works from any working directory and survives package moves. A shared `TestPaths.swift` helper in TestMocks would fix all of them at once.

[migrated] test: MCPLifecycleTests FD leak flaky — delta 9 vs threshold 6 (the-record #307)
## Summary

MCPLifecycleTests checks file descriptor count before/after and fails when delta exceeds threshold (6). The delta sometimes hits 9, indicating a real FD leak in MCP subprocess lifecycle.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `swift test --filter MCPLifecycle` in parallel mode
2. **Observe:** assertion at line ~126 fails: `FD delta 9 > threshold 6`

## Expected Behavior

FD delta after MCP lifecycle test is ≤ 2 (stdin + stdout of the subprocess, both closed).

## Actual Behavior

Delta of 9 suggests 3 MCP subprocess pipe pairs (stdin/stdout/stderr × 3 = 9 FDs) are leaked — likely from processes that were started but not properly terminated via `Process.terminate()` + `Process.waitUntilExit()`.

## Root Cause

MCPSummarizationPlugin spawns external processes via `Process()`. If the test tears down before the process exits, pipe file descriptors are leaked. The `deinit` path may not call `terminate()` on all spawned processes.

## Affected Files

- Record-ML/Tests/Unit/MCPLifecycleTests.swift:126 — assertion
- Record-ML/Sources/MLInfrastructure/Summarization/MCPSummarizationPlugin.swift — subprocess lifecycle
- Record-ML/Sources/MLInfrastructure/MCP/GenericMCPProvider.swift — process management

## Acceptance Criteria

I'm noticing that both `deinit` and `shutdown()` close the pipe handles and call `terminate()` on the process, but they're missing a call to `waitUntilExit()`. The issue is that `terminate()` sends SIGTERM asynchronously and doesn't actually wait for the process to exit or clean up the zombie process — that only happens when `waitUntilExit()` is called or when Foundation's internal termination handler eventually reaps the child.

Foundation's Process class does have internal machinery (a dispatch source on Darwin or a thread in swift-corelibs) that eventually reaps the child, so you don't strictly need `waitUntilExit()` to avoid zombies. The real problem here is likely the test itself: across the 5 load/shutdown cycles, the plugin instances are being dropped expecting their `deinit` to close the pipes immediately, but since these are actors, their `deinit` can be delayed by Swift's ARC and any pending async work. This means the file descriptors aren't getting closed synchronously when expected, causing them to linger across multiple cycles and creating that FD delta.

The test comment acknowledges this reasoning — a real per-cycle leak would cascade to 20+ FDs over 5 cycles, so bumping the threshold to 12 is treating the measured 9 delta as noise from parallel test execution rather than a genuine leak. But that's an assumption that was never verified with an actual code fix. I shouldn't close #138 as fixed based on this threshold change alone; instead, I need to keep it open, narrow V6 to just #189 (which is a real path fix), and flag #138 for proper follow-up investigation.

content.thinking:
The test calls `shutdown()` each cycle, which closes pipes and sends SIGTERM to the process, but it never waits for the process to actually exit. This could leave zombie processes temporarily, though they wouldn't hold file descriptors in our process—just a PID slot. Since `/bin/sleep 60` should exit almost immediately when it receives SIGTERM, this shouldn't be a practical issue.

However, Foundation's Process class internally uses a dispatch source or kqueue to monitor the child process, and that monitoring mechanism itself holds an FD until the process is reaped. Without calling `waitUntilExit()` or registering a termination handler, Foundation might leave that internal monitoring FD open asynchronously, creating a race condition where rapid cycles could transiently accumulate a few FDs before they're cleaned up—especially if reaping happens on a background thread with some delay. The 300ms sleep before measuring should normally give enough time for the process to exit and be reaped, but if it's still measuring 9, that leaves real ambiguity about whether there's a genuine partial leak or just inherent jitter.

Without deeper testing, the honest approach is to avoid silently raising the threshold and instead keep the issue open, ideally adding `waitUntilExit()` as a proper fix.

---
name: feedback-parallel-swift-build-corruption
description: Concurrent swift build/test in the same worktree corrupts shared .build cache — serialize or isolate
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Running multiple agents' `swift build`/`swift test` concurrently in the same git worktree (single root Package.swift monorepo) produces spurious, non-deterministic errors like "no such module 'Alignment'" — a target that builds cleanly standalone (`swift build --target Alignment` succeeds) and that no agent touched. Retrying the same command minutes later, still with other agents' builds in flight, reproduces the same spurious failure; the errors are not real regressions.

**Why:** SwiftPM's incremental build state (`.build/`) at the repo root is shared across every package in this monorepo (see [[project-monorepo]]). Two `swift test` invocations from sibling agents — even against unrelated packages/files — both compile through the same shared dependency graph and write to the same `.build` directory simultaneously, corrupting each other's partial module-cache state mid-build.

**How to apply:** When dispatching parallel Wave-style agents (mega-remediation plan, [[datum-3round-adversarial-review]]-style fleets) that each run `swift test` in this repo, do not trust a spot-check build failure at face value while sibling agents are still running — check for other in-flight agents first, and re-verify with `swift build --target <affected>` standalone before concluding a real regression. Prefer serializing test runs (one agent's tests finish before the next starts) or wait until all agents in the current fan-out have completed before doing final verification builds. The plan's own "lane rule" (only one agent runs tests in a *given package* at a time) is necessary but not sufficient — this monorepo's single shared root Package.swift means it's really "one agent runs `swift build`/`swift test` anywhere in the repo at a time" for build-cache safety, even across different packages.

When building from the root Package.swift, Alignment and RecordPro are sibling targets in the same graph and resolve cleanly, but when building from Record-App's separate manifest with its own dependency chain, SwiftPM might struggle with diamond dependencies or conflicting paths to the same package, causing intermittent failures depending on build order.

Since the root build succeeded but the nested Record-App build failed, the two package graphs are out of sync—this is a pre-existing structural problem unrelated to the recent changes. The pragmatic fix is to run tests from the repository root using the unified package graph instead of cd-ing into subdirectories, which should sidestep the nested-manifest resolution issue.

---
name: feedback-parallel-swift-build-corruption
description: Concurrent swift build/test in the same worktree corrupts shared .build cache — serialize or isolate
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 7c35d465-d5ef-477e-a940-9baf3548f83d
---

Running multiple agents' `swift build`/`swift test` concurrently in the same git worktree (single root Package.swift monorepo) produces spurious, non-deterministic errors like "no such module 'Alignment'" — a target that builds cleanly standalone (`swift build --target Alignment` succeeds) and that no agent touched. Retrying the same command minutes later, still with other agents' builds in flight, reproduces the same spurious failure; the errors are not real regressions.

**Why:** SwiftPM's incremental build state (`.build/`) at the repo root is shared across every package in this monorepo (see [[project-monorepo]]). Two `swift test` invocations from sibling agents — even against unrelated packages/files — both compile through the same shared dependency graph and write to the same `.build` directory simultaneously, corrupting each other's partial module-cache state mid-build.

**How to apply:** When dispatching parallel Wave-style agents (mega-remediation plan, [[datum-3round-adversarial-review]]-style fleets) that each run `swift test` in this repo, do not trust a spot-check build failure at face value while sibling agents are still running — check for other in-flight agents first, and re-verify with `swift build --target <affected>` standalone before concluding a real regression. Prefer serializing test runs (one agent's tests finish before the next starts) or wait until all agents in the current fan-out have completed before doing final verification builds. The plan's own "lane rule" (only one agent runs tests in a *given package* at a time) is necessary but not sufficient — this monorepo's single shared root Package.swift means it's really "one agent runs `swift build`/`swift test` anywhere in the repo at a time" for build-cache safety, even across different packages.

**What's wrong.** `attachDiarization` upserts segments via `GRDBSQL.upsertSegment`, whose `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` sets text/speaker/start/end/confidence but **not `word_timings`** — and `DiarizedSegment.wordTimings` from the incoming transcript is never written. `getSegments` reads `word_timings` back and attaches it to whatever text now occupies that `segment_index`.

**Why it matters.** After any re-diarization (repair pipeline, cleanup pass), segment N's text/boundaries change but its old `word_timings` JSON remains → word-level highlighting/alignment silently points at the wrong words.

**Suggested fix.** Either persist `seg.wordTimings` in the upsert (add the column to `upsertSegment` with excluded update), or explicitly `SET word_timings = NULL` on conflict so stale data can't survive.

1	# Mega Remediation: file issues + fix all the things (Sonnet-granular work packets)
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	A full diagnostic session (2026-07-01) root-caused "diarization doesn't work" to a **capture bug**: `CoreAudioTapCaptureActor` reads the input format once at setup (`CoreAudioTapCaptureActorSupport.swift:144`) and has no `AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange` observer, so a mid-session device sample-rate change makes the converter use a stale ratio — production WAVs are time-stretched 1.6–1.9×, corrupting transcription timestamps and diarization alignment. Two more production bugs surfaced: `-mic-cleaned.wav` files are pure digital silence (−180 dB), and `GRDBSQL.upsertSegment` never writes/clears `word_timings` (stale timings survive re-diarization).
6	
7	The same session fixed all test suites (Record-ML now 314/314 green, uncommitted) and triaged ~55 open issues. Verification against main shows **several open issues are already fixed** (#190, #191, #193, #194, #205, most of F22) — they need regression-test-and-close, not fixes. The user folded **Epic 30** (#202, audit findings F1–F27 from `docs/codebase-audit-20260612-142636.md`) and the **contract-audit criticals** (#211–#213) into this plan. The prior Epic 30 plan (`~/.claude/plans/atomic-roaming-graham.md`) is the spec source for F-numbers but predates the GRDB migration — file paths below are corrected to current main.
8	
9	**Goal**: every packet is small enough for a Sonnet agent to execute alone: one fix, explicit files, verify-first, TDD, one commit.
10	
11	## Ground rules (embed in every agent prompt)
12	
13	- **Scope**: touch ONLY the files listed in your packet. If the fix genuinely requires another file, stop and report back instead of editing it.
14	- **Verify first**: confirm the defect still exists on main before writing code. If already fixed, write the missing regression test (if any), then report `ALREADY_FIXED` with file:line evidence — do not "improve" working code.
15	- **Independent spot-check before closing on ALREADY_FIXED/OBSOLETE**: a second agent (or the orchestrator directly) re-reads the cited file:line evidence and re-runs the regression test independently, without seeing the first agent's conclusion beforehand, before any issue is closed on an `ALREADY_FIXED`, `OBSOLETE_POST_GRDB`, or similar verdict. If the second check disagrees, treat it as a normal packet failure — reopen with the discrepancy and route to a new fix packet, do not close.
16	- **TDD**: failing test first (RED), confirm failure via the package's `swift test --filter`, then implement (GREEN). Swift Testing (`@Test`/`#expect`), not XCTest.
17	- **Layering**: Domain → Foundation only; Business → Domain; Presentation never imports Infrastructure. File caps: Domain 100 / Business 300 / Infrastructure 300 / ViewModels 200 / Views 150 lines.
18	- **Impact check**: before editing a symbol, find its callers (`gitnexus_impact` if available, else grep) and list them in your report.
19	- **Commits**: one commit per fix, format `fix(scope): description (#issue)`. No Claude/Anthropic attribution. Never touch theme files (`Record-Presentation/Sources/Presentation/Theme/`, `Resources/`, `*Theme*Tests`).
20	- **gh**: always `unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh …`.
21	- **Tests per package**: `cd <pkg> && swift test` for Record-Foundation/Record-Audio/Record-ML; root `swift test` for the rest. Only ONE agent runs tests in a given package at a time (lane rule).
22	- **Model**: Sonnet for all packets unless marked `[main-loop]` (done by the orchestrator directly).
23	
24	## Pre-execution adversarial findings (fleet pre-mortem, 2026-07-01)
25	
26	A fleet of adversarial reviewers pre-mortemed this plan before execution started. Every finding below was independently verified against current main. Fixes are applied inline at each packet's bullet below (search for "Pre-flight (fleet pre-mortem)"); this section is the index.
27	
28	- **P4 & E4**: Both packets edit `AppAssemblerBuilders.swift` in different functions (P4 at `:227` inside `buildMenuBarVM`, E4 at `:128` inside `buildMCPProviders`), but Wave 4 is only marked "parallel to Waves 2–3" — the plan's only cross-wave collision note covers Wave 6 → Wave 5 (E4), not Wave 4 (P4) → Wave 5 (E4). Fix: P4 must land (commit) before E4 starts even though their lanes are otherwise parallel.

# Mega Remediation: file issues + fix all the things (Sonnet-granular work packets)

## Context

A full diagnostic session (2026-07-01) root-caused "diarization doesn't work" to a **capture bug**: `CoreAudioTapCaptureActor` reads the input format once at setup (`CoreAudioTapCaptureActorSupport.swift:144`) and has no `AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange` observer, so a mid-session device sample-rate change makes the converter use a stale ratio — production WAVs are time-stretched 1.6–1.9×, corrupting transcription timestamps and diarization alignment. Two more production bugs surfaced: `-mic-cleaned.wav` files are pure digital silence (−180 dB), and `GRDBSQL.upsertSegment` never writes/clears `word_timings` (stale timings survive re-diarization).

The same session fixed all test suites (Record-ML now 314/314 green, uncommitted) and triaged ~55 open issues. Verification against main shows **several open issues are already fixed** (#190, #191, #193, #194, #205, most of F22) — they need regression-test-and-close, not fixes. The user folded **Epic 30** (#202, audit findings F1–F27 from `docs/codebase-audit-20260612-142636.md`) and the **contract-audit criticals** (#211–#213) into this plan. The prior Epic 30 plan (`~/.claude/plans/atomic-roaming-graham.md`) is the spec source for F-numbers but predates the GRDB migration — file paths below are corrected to current main.

**Goal**: every packet is small enough for a Sonnet agent to execute alone: one fix, explicit files, verify-first, TDD, one commit.

## Ground rules (embed in every agent prompt)

- **Scope**: touch ONLY the files listed in your packet. If the fix genuinely requires another file, stop and report back instead of editing it.
- **Verify first**: confirm the defect still exists on main before writing code. If already fixed, write the missing regression test (if any), then report `ALREADY_FIXED` with file:line evidence — do not "improve" working code.
- **Independent spot-check before closing on ALREADY_FIXED/OBSOLETE**: a second agent (or the orchestrator directly) re-reads the cited file:line evidence and re-runs the regression test independently, without seeing the first agent's conclusion beforehand, before any issue is closed on an `ALREADY_FIXED`, `OBSOLETE_POST_GRDB`, or similar verdict. If the second check disagrees, treat it as a normal packet failure — reopen with the discrepancy and route to a new fix packet, do not close.
- **TDD**: failing test first (RED), confirm failure via the package's `swift test --filter`, then implement (GREEN). Swift Testing (`@Test`/`#expect`), not XCTest.
- **Layering**: Domain → Foundation only; Business → Domain; Presentation never imports Infrastructure. File caps: Domain 100 / Business 300 / Infrastructure 300 / ViewModels 200 / Views 150 lines.
- **Impact check**: before editing a symbol, find its callers (`gitnexus_impact` if available, else grep) and list them in your report.
- **Commits**: one commit per fix, format `fix(scope): description (#issue)`. No Claude/Anthropic attribution. Never touch theme files (`Record-Presentation/Sources/Presentation/Theme/`, `Resources/`, `*Theme*Tests`).
- **gh**: always `unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh …`.
- **Tests per package**: `cd <pkg> && swift test` for Record-Foundation/Record-Audio/Record-ML; root `swift test` for the rest. Only ONE agent runs tests in a given package at a time (lane rule).
- **Model**: Sonnet for all packets unless marked `[main-loop]` (done by the orchestrator directly).

## Pre-execution adversarial findings (fleet pre-mortem, 2026-07-01)

A fleet of adversarial reviewers pre-mortemed this plan before execution started. Every finding below was independently verified against current main. Fixes are applied inline at each packet's bullet below (search for "Pre-flight (fleet pre-mortem)"); this section is the index.

## Orchestration mechanics

- **Canary first** (pre-flight rule): run V5 (#205 verify-and-close, smallest packet) alone; on success launch the rest of Wave 1 in parallel, then start lanes.
- Lanes = packages; packets within a lane run serially (build-dir + file contention), lanes run in parallel (max 4 concurrent agents).
- Agents get: the ground-rules block, their packet spec verbatim, exact file paths, and the package test command. `model: sonnet` on every Agent call.
- Orchestrator (main loop) reviews each agent's report + diff before the next packet in that lane starts; failed packets get one retry with the error trace, then escalate to Opus/main-loop.
- Everything stays local on `fix/mega-remediation-20260701` — no push/PR unless the user asks.

**A3 — F11: `stop()` duration from `wavWriter.totalSamplesWritten`, not wall clock.** Files: `CoreAudioTapCaptureActor.swift` (~:265). Remove `try? … ?? 0` / `?? Date()` silent fallbacks (DPS-204). Note: after A1 lands, samples-written is the honest duration even across rate changes.

**A4 — F27: create WAVWriter inside the `do` block** so failed starts don't orphan 44-byte WAVs. Files: `CoreAudioTapCaptureActor.swift:95–101` (note the existing `defer state` guard at :89–92 — keep it correct).

**A5 — #223: `abortRouteChange(with:)` dead code — wire it, don't delete it.**
Files: `MicCaptureActorRouteChange.swift`. It performs the *complete* cleanup (observer removal, voice-processing off, engine teardown) that `handleConfigurationChange()`'s three failure paths skip (they only set state + finish continuation, leaking observer/engine). Replace those failure paths with `abortRouteChange(with:)` calls. RED: source-inspection test that failure paths call it.

Files: `AECProcessorActor.swift`, `WAVCleanedAudioSink.swift`, the far-end feed site (`RecordingStateViewModelStreaming.swift` — read-only for diagnosis), integration test file.

## A6 Investigation Report — Silent mic-cleaned WAV (#245)

**(a) Self-cancellation hypothesis: reproduced and confirmed, with RMS numbers.**

Two synthetic-signal tests in `Record-Audio/Tests/Unit/AECSilentOutputInvestigationTests.swift`, both feeding a continuous 440Hz mic sine wave through `AECProcessorActor` for 280 frames (200 warm-up + 80 tail, mirroring the existing R5 fixture's convergence budget):

- **Scenario 1 (silent far-end reference):** tail RMS **0.05102** — healthy, audible output. AEC's basic pass-through when there's nothing to cancel is fine.
- **Scenario 2 (far-end reference = mic's own signal, no delay):** tail RMS **0.00003**, with the new diagnostic counter reaching **229 consecutive** near-zero-output frames. Output collapses ~1700x relative to scenario 1.

This confirms: if the far-end reference is ever the mic's own signal, Speex correctly (by design) drives output to near-silence. That is correct AEC math given garbage/self-referential input, not a bug in `AECProcessorActor.swift`.

**(b) Root cause outside file scope.** I read `Record-Presentation/Sources/Presentation/ViewModels/RecordingStateViewModelStreaming.swift:106-160` and `RecordingStateViewModelHelpers.swift:15-32` (read-only, not edited). Found **no static code-level aliasing bug**: `nearestSystemFrame()` binary-searches `systemAudioRingBuffer`, which is populated *exclusively* from the `.system`-track stream in `startLiveStream(bufferStream:)` (line 72) — mic frames never enter that buffer. When no system stream is available, it correctly falls back to `TaggedAudioBuffer.silentFarEnd(matching:)` (all-zero), which scenario 1 proves is safe, not the silence bug. If self-cancellation is the real-world cause, the wiring bug (if any) is further upstream — in how the system-audio capture source itself is sourced/routed (`StartRecordingUseCase.getSystemStream()` / the underlying `AudioCaptureEngine` implementation, e.g. `CoreAudioTapCaptureActor`) — not confirmed by static reading, would need live-device investigation. Recommend a follow-up packet against the audio-capture layer.

**(c) Committed:** one commit `82af454d fix(record-audio): log-once diagnostic guard for silent AEC output (#245)` — touches only `AECProcessorActor.swift` (production guard: tracks consecutive near-zero-output frames despite loud mic input, logs once after ~800ms via `logger.error`, resets on `stop()` and on recovery) and the new test file. `WAVCleanedAudioSink.swift` needed no change (writer chain confirmed healthy per A1-A5). **Needs follow-up:** an issue/packet to investigate the system-audio capture source for possible mic/system aliasing at the ScreenCaptureKit/CoreAudio layer.

**(d) RED/GREEN:** all 4 new tests written and run GREEN on first pass after two build fixes (OSLog string concatenation via `+` doesn't compile — combined into single interpolated literals; `#expect` comment argument can't be built via `+` either — same fix).

**(e) Full Record-Audio suite: 177/177 tests passed, 29/29 suites passed.** SwiftLint clean (0 violations) on both touched files after renaming the test type to fit the 40-char limit and replacing a 3-tuple return with a named `SineFixtureResult` struct.</result>

Per this repo's `.claude/rules/no-embedded-languages.md`: SQL lives in dedicated `*SQL.swift` files as caseless enums with static functions — `GRDBSQL.swift` already follows this pattern, keep it that way, do not inline SQL elsewhere.

RED test: attach diarization twice with different word_timings on the same segment → second read must return the SECOND timings (not the stale first). Also test: attach with nil wordTimings → stored value is NULL (not stale from a prior non-nil attach).

Fix: add `word_timings` to `upsertSegment`'s INSERT + `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... excluded.word_timings` clause. At the `attachDiarization` call site (`GRDBStorageActor+Diarization.swift`), encode `seg.wordTimings` via `JSONEncoder` (nil → SQL NULL, not an empty string or missing bind).

Per this repo's `.claude/rules/no-embedded-languages.md`: SQL lives in dedicated `*SQL.swift` files as caseless enums with static functions — `GRDBSQL.swift` already follows this pattern, keep it that way, do not inline SQL elsewhere.

RED test: attach diarization twice with different word_timings on the same segment → second read must return the SECOND timings (not the stale first). Also test: attach with nil wordTimings → stored value is NULL (not stale from a prior non-nil attach).

## Final report

Verdict, commit hash, file:line evidence (both the SQL change and the encode-at-call-site change), RED/GREEN summary, callers of `upsertSegment`/`attachDiarization` found via impact check, full Record-ML test suite pass/fail count. ~200-300 words.

    public func attachDiarization(id: RecordingID, diarization: DiarizedTranscript) async throws {

        await Task.yield()
        let encoder = JSONEncoder()

            try await dbPool.write { db in

                for (idx, seg) in diarization.segments.enumerated() {
                    let wordTimingsJSON: String?

                        id.rawValue, idx, seg.text, seg.speakerId.rawValue,
                        seg.startTime, seg.endTime, seg.confidence, wordTimingsJSON,

---
name: feedback-parallel-swift-build-corruption
description: Concurrent swift build/test in the same worktree corrupts shared .build cache — serialize or isolate
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 7c35d465-d5ef-477e-a940-9baf3548f83d
---

Running multiple agents' `swift build`/`swift test` concurrently in the same git worktree (single root Package.swift monorepo) produces spurious, non-deterministic errors like "no such module 'Alignment'" — a target that builds cleanly standalone (`swift build --target Alignment` succeeds) and that no agent touched. Retrying the same command minutes later, still with other agents' builds in flight, reproduces the same spurious failure; the errors are not real regressions.

**Why:** SwiftPM's incremental build state (`.build/`) at the repo root is shared across every package in this monorepo (see [[project-monorepo]]). Two `swift test` invocations from sibling agents — even against unrelated packages/files — both compile through the same shared dependency graph and write to the same `.build` directory simultaneously, corrupting each other's partial module-cache state mid-build.

**How to apply:** When dispatching parallel Wave-style agents (mega-remediation plan, [[datum-3round-adversarial-review]]-style fleets) that each run `swift test` in this repo, do not trust a spot-check build failure at face value while sibling agents are still running — check for other in-flight agents first, and re-verify with `swift build --target <affected>` standalone before concluding a real regression. Prefer serializing test runs (one agent's tests finish before the next starts) or wait until all agents in the current fan-out have completed before doing final verification builds. The plan's own "lane rule" (only one agent runs tests in a *given package* at a time) is necessary but not sufficient — this monorepo's single shared root Package.swift means it's really "one agent runs `swift build`/`swift test` anywhere in the repo at a time" for build-cache safety, even across different packages.

**What's wrong.** `attachDiarization` upserts segments via `GRDBSQL.upsertSegment`, whose `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` sets text/speaker/start/end/confidence but **not `word_timings`** — and `DiarizedSegment.wordTimings` from the incoming transcript is never written. `getSegments` reads `word_timings` back and attaches it to whatever text now occupies that `segment_index`.

**Why it matters.** After any re-diarization (repair pipeline, cleanup pass), segment N's text/boundaries change but its old `word_timings` JSON remains → word-level highlighting/alignment silently points at the wrong words.

**Suggested fix.** Either persist `seg.wordTimings` in the upsert (add the column to `upsertSegment` with excluded update), or explicitly `SET word_timings = NULL` on conflict so stale data can't survive.
